snippet_text: What is lambda function in Python? Anonymous function defined with lambda keyword.
What are functions in Python? Functions are blocks of reusable code defined using def keyword.
What is the difference between bytes, bytearray, and memoryview? bytes are immutable sequences of bytes, bytearray is mutable, memoryview provides a view into binary
What is Python's with statement? Used for resource management, ensures proper closing (e.g., with files).
What is enumerate() in Python? Returns index and value while iterating over a sequence.
What are Python lists? Ordered, mutable collections of elements.
What is method overriding in Python? Providing a new implementation of a parent class method in a child class.
How do you create thread-safe code in Python? By using locks, semaphores, queues, or atomic operations from threading module.
What is the difference between generator and iterator in Python? Generators are a type of iterator created with yield, while iterators can be built with classes.
What is the difference between syntax error and runtime error? Syntax error occurs before execution, runtime error occurs during execution.
What is the difference between staticmethod, classmethod, and instancemethod? @staticmethod doesn’t take self or cls; @classmethod takes cls; instance methods take self.
What is the difference between == and is in Python? == checks value equality, is checks identity (whether two variables point to the same object).
What is len() function in Python? Returns the length of a sequence or collection.
How do you declare a variable in Python? Just assign a value: x = 10, y = "Hello".
What are default arguments in functions? Arguments that assume a default value if not provided during function call.
What is encapsulation in Python? Encapsulation means restricting direct access to variables and methods to protect data.
How do you optimize Python code for performance? Techniques: use built-in functions, list comprehensions, generators, NumPy for numerical operations,
What are Python comprehensions? Compact syntax for creating lists, sets, and dictionaries.
What are destructors in Python? Destructors (__del__) are called when an object is deleted or goes out of scope.
What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous code execution? Synchronous waits for tasks sequentially; asynchronous allows overlapping tasks, improving efficienc
What is string concatenation in Python? Joining strings using + operator or join() method.
What is the difference between yield and return in Python? yield pauses a function and returns a generator; return ends the function and returns a value.
What is __name__ == "__main__" in Python? It ensures that code runs only when the script is executed directly, not when imported.
Explain how Python handles function overloading. Python doesn’t support traditional overloading; instead, default arguments or *args/**kwargs are use

In a singly linked list, what does each node contain? Data and a pointer to the next node.
How do you perform topological sorting in a DAG? By using Kahn’s algorithm (BFS) or DFS finishing times.
What is level order traversal? Visiting nodes of a tree level by level using a queue.
What is the maximum number of nodes at level k in a binary tree? 2k.

What is double hashing? A collision resolution method using a second hash function to calculate probe sequence.
How do you find the number of islands in a grid? By using DFS or BFS traversal marking visited cells.
What is a binary heap and why is it efficient? It is a complete binary tree used for priority queues, offering O(log n) insert and delete.
What is the time complexity to search a word in a trie? O(L), where L is the length of the word.
How do you implement a trie to store a large dictionary of words? Each node represents characters with children pointers, storing isEnd flag for complete words.
How is a queue different from a stack? Queue uses FIFO while stack uses LIFO.
What is the best-case time complexity for searching in a BST? O(log n).
Define a stack in one line. Stack is a linear structure where elements are pushed and popped from one end.
What is the head in a linked list? The first node of the linked list.
What is a deque? A double-ended queue where insertion and deletion are possible from both ends.
What is the algorithm to reverse nodes in k-group in a linked list? Reverse k nodes iteratively, then connect recursively for remaining nodes.
How do you build a heap from an array? By applying heapify bottom-up in O(n) time.
How do you implement two stacks in one array? Divide the array into two parts or let them grow from opposite ends.
How do you find the longest palindromic substring? By expanding around centers or using dynamic programming.
What problem occurs in hash tables when two keys map to the same index? Collision.
How do you find bridges in a graph? By DFS with discovery and low values to identify critical edges.
What does dynamic array mean? An array that can resize automatically when full.
How do you implement Kruskal’s algorithm for MST? By sorting edges and applying union-find to avoid cycles.
How do you implement Rabin-Karp algorithm? By hashing substrings with rolling hash for efficient string search.
When would you increase input resolution and when would you decrease it? Increase for small/far objects; decrease for speed/memory limits.

How is Exclusive Feature Bundling implemented internally? Groups sparse, mutually exclusive features into one bin.

What is the benefit of BN? Stabilizes and speeds up training.

What is TF-IDF? Weights words by importance.

What is stemming? PorterStemmer or LancasterStemmer.
